branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Platform partially or fully rolls back the recommendation change for educational content ranking.
branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Platform messaging shifts from defending optimization to announcing recalibration, restored distribution, or pilot reversal.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Visible evidence pooling shows broad creator harm and legitimacy costs exceed platform reversal costs.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Platform launches a transparency dashboard or more detailed reporting while preserving most recommendation logic.
branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: New creator-facing metrics, category explanations, or periodic governance reports appear without full rollback.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Platform seeks legitimacy repair without conceding core ranking authority.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: A notable subset of educational creators diversifies away, reduces posting, or exits the platform ecosystem.
branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Sustained posting declines, public migration announcements, or increasing references to alternate distribution channels.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Coalition fails to gain concessions and creators conclude reach loss is durable.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Advertisers privately or publicly pressure the platform to improve transparency, restore variety, or stabilize trust.
branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Agency/account-team escalations, spend reallocation signals, or advertiser-linked requests for governance clarification.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Brand buyers infer that legitimacy controversy or repetitive inventory harms campaign value.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: No major concession occurs; creators remain dissatisfied but fragmented, and viewers adapt to the new feed.
branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Complaint volume persists without coordinated escalation, policy reversal, or meaningful dashboard changes.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Platform opacity remains defensible enough and creator coordination remains below action threshold.

blockers: Lack of externally validated harm data
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A transparency package without ranking change does not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: The platform materially reverses or recalibrates the recommendation policy so that small educational creators recover meaningful distribution relative to the post-change baseline.
endpoint_ledger.label: Platform rollback or recalibration

meta.important_question: Will the platform materially reverse or recalibrate the recommendation change in a way that restores reach for small educational creators?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Platform authority is high enough to act, but reversal costs and opacity norms make this uncertain.
realization_criteria: Platform publicly announces rollback, category-specific recalibration, or equivalent policy reversal.
Creator-side analytics show sustained reach recovery across a broad affected sample relative to immediate post-change levels.
Platform messaging acknowledges a substantive recommendation adjustment rather than only communications changes.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Rollback is explicitly named as a branch, but no concession has occurred at T0.

blockers: Fear that transparency invites further challenge
Resource and precedent costs of ongoing disclosure
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Generic PR statements or one-off vague metrics do not satisfy this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: The platform introduces a dashboard or equivalent disclosure system that provides actionable clarity on recommendation impacts and category treatment.
endpoint_ledger.label: Meaningful transparency disclosure

meta.important_question: Will the platform provide a meaningful transparency dashboard or equivalent disclosure that clarifies recommendation impacts beyond vague metrics?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Legitimacy repair pressures support this option even if the platform preserves substantive control.
realization_criteria: Platform releases creator-facing dashboard, detailed category metrics, or regular governance reporting beyond vague summary metrics.
Disclosures include enough specificity to compare educational creator performance or recommendation treatment over time.
Affected creators or advertisers can cite new platform-provided data as decision-relevant evidence.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Transparency dashboard is an explicit branch and a lower-cost concession than rollback.

blockers: Fragmentation between exit-minded and loyalist creators
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: High complaint volume from isolated individuals without coordination does not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Affected small educational creators maintain a coordinated, visible coalition capable of exerting continuing legitimacy pressure on the platform.
endpoint_ledger.label: Durable creator coalition

meta.important_question: Will the affected creator coalition sustain enough participation and visibility to remain a credible pressure bloc rather than fragmenting?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint matters because many other branches depend on coalition persistence.
realization_criteria: Coalition retains recurring participation from a substantial cross-section of affected creators over multiple ticks.
Public statements, data pooling, or coordinated asks continue without major collapse in engagement.
Platform or advertisers respond to the coalition as a recognized interlocutor.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Coalition durability is explicitly uncertain and central to scenario dynamics.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Routine account conversations without conditional leverage do not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Advertisers move from passive preference expression to concrete pressure that affects platform governance choices.
endpoint_ledger.label: Advertiser pressure realized

meta.important_question: Will advertisers convert brand safety and legitimacy concerns into concrete pressure on the platform?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Advertisers have moderate leverage due to revenue dependence, but activation thresholds are not yet crossed.
realization_criteria: Advertisers or agencies request policy clarification, transparency, or inventory changes tied to spend decisions.
Platform communications or internal decisions explicitly respond to advertiser concern.
Observable spend threats, reallocations, or account escalations occur.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Advertiser pressure is an explicit branch but remains latent at T0.

blockers: Hope for rollback or transparency concession
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Private exploration of alternatives without behavioral change does not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: A notable subset of small educational creators reduces reliance on the platform by exiting, cutting output, or shifting effort elsewhere.
endpoint_ledger.label: Creator exit or diversification

meta.important_question: Will a notable share of small educational creators reduce reliance on the platform through exit or meaningful diversification?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Exit is plausible if coalition efforts stall and distribution losses persist.
realization_criteria: A visible subset of affected creators publicly announces migration, reduced posting, or off-platform diversification.
Posting frequency or platform exclusivity declines across enough creators to indicate strategic reallocation rather than isolated frustration.
Coalition discourse shifts from reform demands toward adaptation or departure strategies.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Creator exit is explicitly listed as a branch and is supported by high dependency stress.

merge_hypotheses.mechanism: A limited transparency package could satisfy enough fairness and safety concerns to reduce escalation even without rollback.
Economic dependence and organizer fatigue may pull dissent back into quieter accommodation over time.
If variety complaints do not become salient, audiences may normalize the new exposure mix, stabilizing the platform's position.
A shared framing around quality and safety could align beneficiaries and reduce external pressure unless contrary evidence spreads.

population_archetypes.description: People who consume videos on the platform and experience changes in variety and recommendations.
Small and mid-sized educational creators dependent on platform discovery.
Brand and agency buyers allocating spend based on safety and audience fit.
Teams running official partner channels benefiting from platform certification and promotion.

risk_flags.note: Platform controls key measurement systems, making independent verification of favoritism difficult at T0.
Creator dependence on platform distribution may hide the true scale of private dissatisfaction.
Decision authority over recommendation rules and disclosure is concentrated inside the platform.
Viewer concern about reduced variety may remain too diffuse to sustain broad pressure.
Affected creators may split between reform, resignation, and exit strategies.
Institutional and group names were fictionalized because the scenario concerns platform governance dynamics.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional video platform changes recommendation rules, reducing reach for small educational creators while boosting official partner channels. Small creators suspect favoritism, advertisers prioritize brand safety, viewers perceive lower variety, and the platform offers only vague metrics. T0 centers on exposure shocks, platform authority, creator coalition durability, and unresolved pathways toward rollback, transparency, creator exit, or advertiser pressure.
uncertainty_notes: Exact platform size, geography, and timing are unspecified.
No direct evidence yet confirms intentional favoritism beyond observed reach changes and partner gains.
Advertiser concern is directional and may not yet be organized into explicit pressure.

sociology_baseline.note: Actors update more readily from familiar sources and observed performance data than from distant claims.
Many affected creators need visible peer participation before escalating publicly; viewers have an even higher threshold.
Platform dependency suppresses open dissent among many creators despite private grievance.
Groups mostly exchange validating interpretations within their own networks.
Coalition growth likely requires repeated, cross-validated examples of reach loss and unfair treatment.
Creator identity and partner status shape interpretations of fairness and legitimacy.
Without fresh signals, broad audience and advertiser focus may dissipate quickly.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: A salient policy shift altered exposure patterns, making before-and-after comparisons socially legible.
Vague platform metrics create an evidence vacuum that increases rumor, inference, and legitimacy contests.
Many affected creators depend on platform reach, dampening overt dissent and increasing strategic caution.
Advertiser and platform narratives can justify concentration toward partner channels under a safety rationale.
Perceived decline in content variety can slowly convert private annoyance into public sympathy for creators.

trait_vectors.tendency: protects platform discretion while minimizing concession cost
seeks fairness and visibility but is constrained by platform dependence
supports existing governance while avoiding overt triumphalism
uses quiet leverage unless business or reputational risk rises
reacts to experience changes but often remains diffuse and weakly organized
tries to transform individual grievances into a credible collective case
frames changes as optimization and avoids disclosing sensitive internals
amplifies visible creator narratives faster than formal evidence can accumulate
